That is fine for measuring inference and says nothing about how a model gets on      chain, which is its own problem: a layer of Qwen3-0.6B is 31.5MB, and no      transaction carries 31.5MB of calldata on any chain worth running.      So weights arrive in chunks, each becoming its own contract, and a directory lists      them. A tensor is then a byte range spanning several chunks, which the precompile      stitches back together \u2014 the cost of chunking being that the reader must know the      layout rather than the writer.      Chunk and directory are distinguished by the first byte of the deployed code rather      than by a magic number in the payload.
